body:
## Parent

#98

## What to build

A Skill named Proofread, in the Collection's editorial category, that takes one independently supplied Text Artifact and removes its mechanical language errors without touching anything else. It depends on no peer Skill: it never requires Write or Redline provenance, and it is usable on text that no other Skill has seen.

It is model-invoked, with a description narrow enough to be honest about when it applies. The model may start it only when there is a specific Text Artifact and either an explicit proofreading term or a request unambiguously limited to mechanical language errors. Generic requests to edit, rewrite, polish, improve, or review are exclusions, stated as exclusions. A user can also invoke it by name at any time, which is how its conservative contract stays directly reachable.

It resolves one parameter, the language, and resolves it by the Collection's precedence: the Formal Invocation first, then a recognized Kntnt Handoff Metadata map if the Text Artifact carries one, then the current Contextual Instruction, then applicable Conversation Context, then inference from the Text Artifact, then the default, which is the language of the supplied text. Materially ambiguous or mixed language is clarified rather than guessed. Unrelated document frontmatter is never interpreted as Kntnt configuration, and the Skill preserves all frontmatter byte-for-byte apart from consuming a language value it is entitled to read. Recognized metadata that is unusable and not suppressed by a higher-precedence formal value is reported as unusable artifact metadata rather than silently reinterpreted. With the language settled, it loads that Language Resource's mechanics scope and nothing else.

What it corrects is the objective mechanical layer: spelling, grammar, punctuation, agreement, inflection, duplicated and missing words, and locale mechanics. What it preserves is everything else — wording, meaning, tone, register, structure, factual content, formatting, code, and metadata — and where several forms are valid it preserves the original, because preference is not error. Requesting mechanical correction never becomes an unsolicited rewrite. No spellchecker, grammar service, or bespoke mechanical scanner is introduced; correction stays model-based.

One invocation processes exactly one Text Artifact; more than one is refused rather than resolved into per-file configuration. Delivery follows the Collection's shared output contract, including In-place Editing and its refusals, and the short no-change status when nothing was corrected. The Skill ships under every convention the Collection already holds every Skill to: the Invocation Envelope section, help routing, the strict-grammar refusal that names the problem and prints the relevant synopsis, the dependency preamble and declaration lists for the runtime the shared resolver needs, the Codex sidecar mirroring its invocation policy, a README section, a Catalog entry, and a current digest.

Because this Skill is model-invocable, two places that today name a single model-invocable Skill stop describing the collection accurately, and both are part of this ticket. One is the sentence in the Skills coding standard motivating why both invocation fields are always written. The other is the assertion message of `test_agents_md_is_model_invoked` in `tests/test_kntnt.py`: the assertion itself stays true and stays green, and only its explanation of why goes stale, which is exactly the kind of drift a green run hides.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Proofread ships as a Skill in the Collection's editorial category, created if the category does not yet exist, and declares no peer Skill dependency.
- [ ] Its description permits model invocation only for a specific Text Artifact plus an explicit proofreading term or an unambiguous limitation to mechanical language errors, and names generic editing, rewriting, polishing, improving, and reviewing as exclusions.
- [ ] Its frontmatter and Codex sidecar agree that a model may start it, and both fields are written rather than left to a default.
- [ ] Invocation by name works and applies the same contract.
- [ ] The Formal Invocation accepts a language option, an output option, an in-place option, and one Text Artifact argument or reference; the boolean vocabulary and defaults match the Collection's other editorial grammar.
- [ ] Language resolves by the fixed precedence, ending at the language of the supplied text; ambiguous or mixed language is clarified rather than guessed.
- [ ] Only the mechanics scope of the resolved Language Resource is loaded; no composition, review, or anti-slop guidance is read.
- [ ] Spelling, grammar, punctuation, agreement, inflection, duplicated or missing words, and locale mechanics are corrected.
- [ ] Wording, meaning, tone, structure, factual content, formatting, code, and metadata are preserved, and the original is kept wherever several forms are valid.
- [ ] Unrelated document frontmatter is never read as Kntnt configuration, and frontmatter is otherwise preserved byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Unusable recognized metadata is reported as such when no formal value supersedes it.
- [ ] More than one Text Artifact in one invocation is refused.
- [ ] Delivery follows the shared output contract, including In-place Editing, its refusals, the collision rule, and the no-change status in the Text Artifact's language.
- [ ] Malformed flags, invalid booleans, contradictory output choices, and flags with no work to do are refused before any side effect, following the Collection's diagnostic and help conventions.
- [ ] The Skill ships its Invocation Envelope section, help page with the required sections and option parity, dependency declarations and preamble, compatibility statement, Codex sidecar, README section, Catalog entry, and current digest.
- [ ] The sentence in the Skills coding standard naming the only model-invocable Skill is corrected to describe the collection as it now ships.
- [ ] The assertion message of `test_agents_md_is_model_invoked` in `tests/test_kntnt.py` no longer claims its subject is the only Skill a model invokes on its own, while the assertion it explains is left unchanged.
- [ ] The repository's four documented checks pass, and comparison against the Agent Skills reference validator raises no complaint the Collection's recorded deviations do not already account for.

## Blocked by

- #99 — the shared output and In-place Editing contract.
- #100 — the Language Resource contract and resolver.

## Vantage point

Written against commit `4406694`.

title: Proofread corrects mechanics and refuses to become a rewrite
